title: Kernel interleaving phaseplot capture: initial nsight trace and notes
body:
Summary:
This doc captures an exploratory Nsight run aimed at visualizing kernel interleaving and handoff jitter for our microbatcher + CUDA graph execution path. Goal: determine whether tail latency spikes (99.9p) correlate with cross-kernel idle fragments introduced by async copy phasing and kernel launch packing when the KV cache is active. This is a working log — rough plots, hypotheses, and next steps.

Environment and config:
- HW: A100s (80GB) in p3dn-like topology, NVLink enabled. Host: ubuntu-22.04, CUDA 12.2.
- Build: serving-runtime@main + experimental-batcher-rework (PR#1987).
- Model: llama-2-like decoder, sequence len 1024, microbatch=4, pipeline: prefix cache + kv prefetch.
- Capture flags: nsight-cu-cli --trace nvtx, api, kernel, memcpy --capture-range 1:2000 --sampling 10ns. Also captured perf counters: sm_active_cycles, inst_issued, warp_execution_efficiency.

Commands used:
- nvprof replaced by nsight-cli. Example capture: nsight-cu-cli --target-processes all --sample 10ns --csv --output capture-run-A.csv --trace api,kernel,memcopy -- /opt/redwood/bin/serving-runtime --config debug/trace.yaml
- Postprocessing: python tools/phaseplot.py capture-run-A.csv --window 0.2 --agg=per-ms --out=phaseplot-A.png

Quick observations (from phaseplot-A and timeline slices):
1) Recurrent short idle gaps (~120-260us) between kernel groups around token emission steps. These gaps do not line up with host-side CPU stalls, but appear immediately after async memcpy start events.
2) CUDA graph replay shows micro-batches 0..3 scheduled in tight succession, but we observed fragmentation: kernel group i contains 3 small kernels, group i+1 starts ~150us later rather than <30us expected.
3) SM active cycles: average occupancy for the big attention kernel is 62% during steady-state, but drops to 28% during the idle fragments. Warp efficiency drops from 89% to 46% in those periods.
4) Prefetch vs no-prefetch: when KV prefetch is disabled, idle gaps shrink but average latency increases slightly — suggests prefetch scheduling interacts with kernel packing in an adversarial way.

Detailed timeline notes (timestamps relative to capture start):
- 00:00:342.120 ms: asyncMemcpy H2D start (kv prefetch slab 0) -> kernel: small prefetch kernel (lookup) -> expected immediate decoder kernel but delayed by 120-180us.
- 00:00:463.305 ms: decoder-attn-kernel (big) launches, 1.2ms runtime, SM occupancy 64%.
- 00:00:465.630 ms: copy engine starts another async memcpy for microbatch 2, interleaved with attention kernel completion and causing a gap where SMs are idle while copy engine contends for PCIe/NVLink.
- 00:00:701.000 ms: kernel group packing resumed but kernel launch coalescing produced different stream priorities causing reorder.

Hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A (copy-engine contention): concurrent async copies are stealing DMA bandwidth or PCIe/NVLink scheduling slots, introducing micro-pauses that prevent kernels from being enqueued promptly. This aligns with idle gaps coinciding with memcpy start events.
- Hypothesis B (stream priority and launch ordering): different kernels use different CUDA streams with mismatched priorities; kernel groups expected to appear back-to-back are being reordered or delayed due to stream priority preemption.
- Hypothesis C (CUDA graph fragmentation): when recording CUDA graphs across variable-length microbatches + KV cache misses, the graph becomes fragmented into many small nodes; replay scheduling cannot pack launches tightly, leading to scheduling overheads.

Evidence supporting hypotheses:
- We saw DMA engine counters rise during idle fragments and reported NVLink utilization spikes.
- Nsight's API timeline shows many cudaLaunchKernel calls separated by host-side gaps even when capture shows little CPU work.
- When forcing single stream and forcing streamPriority high on the decoder stream, idle fragments decreased in a short repro.

Quick experiments run and immediate results:
1) Single-stream replay: force all kernel launches onto stream 0 during replay. Result: 99.9p tail improved by ~18% in the synthetic trace, idle gaps reduced to ~30us. Side-effect: throughput decreased 4% due to lost overlap on copy/compute.
2) NVLink throttle sim: limited concurrent async memcpy to one outstanding H2D per GPU. Result: latency tail reduced but average token latency rose slightly. Suggests an overlap sweet-spot.
3) CUDA graph grouping: record two variants: (A) monolithic graph per microbatch, (B) per-stage small graphs. Monolithic graph reduced launch overhead but increased memory pressure.

Measurements (representative numbers):
- Baseline (with prefetch, multi-stream): avg token latency 32.8ms, p99 120ms, p99.9 320ms, SM active cycles (attention) 62%.
- Single-stream test: avg 34.1ms, p99 98ms, p99.9 260ms, SM active cycles 60%.
- No-prefetch test: avg 35.5ms, p99 140ms, p99.9 360ms, SM active cycles 68% (because fewer async-copy stalls observed).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to test with real traffic (not synthetic deterministic microbatch phases) to see if fragmentation persists under variable arrival times.
- Capture on different GPU types (H100) to verify whether NVLink vs PCIe behavior changes fragmentation characteristics.
- Correlate with host-side CPU wakeups: ensure we are not missing brief scheduler preemption on the host that pauses enqueueing.
- Add per-stream priority instrumentation and allow dynamic priority tuning in the runtime.

Proposed mitigations to experiment with:
1) Introduce a small software gate between large async memcpys and kernel launches to smooth copy bursts (token-bucket for DMA submissions).
2) Consolidate critical decoder kernels into a high-priority stream and set lower priority for background prefetch kernels. Test dynamic priority inversion if needed.
3) During CUDA graph recording, attempt graph compaction pass that coalesces adjacent small nodes where safe. Consider recording with explicit stream-ordered node grouping.
4) Expose a config knob for max concurrent outstanding async copies per GPU.

Next steps and owners:
- Marco: add per-stream priority toggles in the experimental branch and run capture with priority=high decoder stream (due 2026-08-16).
- Priya: run same repro on an H100 node and compare NVSwitch counters (due 2026-08-18).
- Jun: add light-weight host-side trace to record pthread wakeups and scheduler preemption around enqueue calls (due 2026-08-17).
- Anya (me): implement capture-to-phaseplot automation and add quick dashboard for idle-gap histograms (PR draft 1995).

Appendix: quick notes on tools and scripts used:
- tools/phaseplot.py: aggregates kernel start/stop events into a 2D raster (kernel index vs time) and computes idle-gap quantiles. Output: phaseplot-A.png, gap-hist-A.csv.
- capture-run-A.csv stored on /tmp/captures/; large (1.2GB) — be careful pulling to laptop.
- Useful nsight queries: "nsight-cu-cli --query-processes", and the CSV column "CUDA API:cudaLaunchKernel:start" is what phaseplot.py uses.

If you clone this repro and want to run quickly: checkout serving-runtime@debug/phaseplot, configure trace.yaml with capture.window_ms=800, set TRACE_NVTX=1 and run the provided run_capture.sh. Please add any new captures to the linked_artifacts list with the date in the filename.

Notes-to-self: scribbles in the capture show repeated pattern at 8:17 of the trace that might be correlated with our batcher drift; revisit after adding per-stream tids to NVTX.

End of initial capture notes.
